headlines.summary: SpaceX shares jumped after the company reported surging revenue growth in its third quarter, and owner Elon Musk floated a potential SpaceX-Tesla merger.
headlines.article_text: SpaceX pops 10% after revenue rose 161%, Elon Musk floats Tesla merger Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points SpaceX soared in premarket trading after reporting strong revenue growth and beating estimates. The company pinned the results on its growing AI business, and recurring revenue from its satellite business. Billionaire owner Elon Musk also floated a potential merger with his electric-vehicle firm Tesla. In this article SPCX TSLA CRWV NBIS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk attends the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit at the Institute of Peace on Oct. 8, 2026 in Washington, DC. Win McNamee | Getty Images SpaceX jumped in premarket trading on Wednesday after the company reported surging revenue growth in its third quarter, and owner Elon Musk floated a potential SpaceX- Tesla merger. The space company, which made its debut on the Nasdaq in the biggest IPO ever in June, reported third-quarter revenue on Tuesday of $14.6 billion, up 161% from the previous year, and beating LSEG consensus estimates of $12.72 billion. Meanwhile, its operating income from operations came in at $2.8 billion, with net income of $4.4 billion, after reporting a net loss of $1.05 billion in the same period a year earlier. On the earnings call, Musk said he's considering a combination with Tesla — which would mark the largest merger in history — and that the boards of both companies have created specific committees to discuss a consolidation. "I do think there's a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there's a lot to be gained from cooperating," Musk said on the call. Tesla is set to report third-quarter earnings after the closing bell on Wednesday. SpaceX shares rose 10.4% before the markets opened on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Tesla shares were up 2.1% in premarket trading. Shares of other space stocks, including Rocket Lab , Intuitive Machines , and AST SpaceMobile , were all higher in premarket trading. SpaceX shares since its debut on the Nasdaq. SpaceX forecasts first-quarter 2027 revenue between $33 billion and $37 billion, beating the average analyst estimate of $22.2 billion, per LSEG. "We delivered another strong quarter in Q3. Revenue grew an impressive 161% year-over-year, fueled by continued momentum in Connectivity and a clear inflection in our Super Intelligence business," SpaceX's Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnson said in the earnings release. Johnson pinned the strong results on recurring revenue from its satellite internet business, Starlink , and significant expansion of its Super Intelligence [SI] infrastructure. The company has dived into AI this year, which it's now calling SI. The segment is its largest business unit, with revenue soaring ninefold to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the same quarter last year. Bull case for AI cloud providers Commentary on computing during the earnings call supported "continued pricing power and shorter payback periods" for AI cloud providers, Truist Securities analysts said in a Tuesday note. "Despite market concerns relating to financing for AI cloud providers this past week, we believe SpaceX's third-quarter 2026 represents the first data point during the earnings season to support the bull case for AI cloud providers," they added. watch now VIDEO 1:59 01:59 SpaceX reports revenue beat, stock sees slight gains in extended trading Closing Bell: Overtime They explained that demand appears "insatiable," with SpaceX noting that it could rent out its capacity several times over. The analysts said Coreweave and Nebius are set to benefit and capture demand as "pricing power will more than offset higher rates." The shares of cloud providers including Nebius , Coreweave , Iren , and Applied Digital also rose above 3% in premarket trading on Wednesday following Musk's comments. — Lora Kolodny contributed to this report Choose CNBC as your preferred source on Google and never miss a moment from the most trusted name in business news.
